title: How many leap years come between 2024 and 2099?
description: A leap year is a year that four divides, with an exception for century years. The video lists the years from two thousand and twenty four, counts them, and checks the count with fours.
teaching_notes: One idea: leap years are the years that four divides, found from their last two digits, and the century exception does not apply between 2024 and 2099. Watch for students who count one too few because they leave out the first year.

video_script.why: The child lists the years that four divides between 2024 and 2099 by their last two digits, checks that the century exception does not apply, and counts them.
video_script.substitution: Leap years are the multiples of 4, so list them from 2024 by their last two digits and count the jumps between the first and the last.
video_script.anchor: a calendar page for February with 29 days, and a strip of years from 2024 to 2099

final_answer.spoken: there are nineteen leap years, from two thousand and twenty four to two thousand and ninety six

hold_back: Answer: 19 leap years (2024, 2028, ..., 2096); the first question depends on the year of birth
maths_rules: a leap year is a multiple of 4, except a year divisible by 100 but not by 400
the next century year after 2024 is 2100, which is past 2099, so the exception never applies
the leap years are 2024, 2028, 2032, ..., 2096, with last two digits 24, 28, ..., 96
2096 + 4 = 2100 is past 2099, so 2096 is the last
video_script.design: One idea: list the multiples of four from the first leap year and count the jumps. Callback to the leap years found by their last two digits in the range from 2030 to 2040. Wrong idea: none is broken. The strip of years stays on the board to the end.

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step two, list the years that four divides. Twenty four is six fours, so two thousand and twenty four is the first.

narration: <bookmark mark='gap'/>Step three, count the years. From two thousand and twenty four to two thousand and ninety six is seventy two.
<bookmark mark='jumps'/>Seventy two divided by four is eighteen jumps.
